verdict_scope.included: Classic 1996 English base game, publisher PDF pages 1–12, including every distinct base Action Card explanation.
verdict_scope.method: Fresh independent comparison of the complete supplied summary against the complete supplied authoritative extracted base text and direct text extraction of every PDF page 1–12, including card-face wording. No external sources, prior reports, reader materials, questions or answer keys consulted.
verdict_scope.meaning: PASS means no material inaccurate gameplay claim, unsupported conflict resolution, or important omission relative to these sources was found. It does not certify that the source supplies a definitive procedure for every reachable base-game situation. The existing verification banner is not treated as evidence of a present gameplay defect.

complete_core_verdict_reason: Not complete-core PASS: ordinary base actions can reach states for which the authorized source gives no complete legal execution procedure. Faithfully identifying those gaps preserves source fidelity but does not supply the missing rules. MAJOR here describes unresolved gameplay completeness, not a claim that the summary misquotes the publisher.

source_limitations.description: The King returns requires each player to return three eligible own Caballeros from regions and/or court, excluding the King’s region and Castillo. No shortfall procedure is specified when fewer than three eligible pieces exist.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: An affected player can lack three removable pieces; the summary cannot determine how to finish this action from the source alone.

source_limitations.description: Send one from each player has no fallback when a player has no Caballero in any eligible region. Courts, Castillo and the King’s region are not eligible origins.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: The selecting player may be unable to select the required one piece for a color.

source_limitations.description: Secret removal of two requires a region containing at least two own Caballeros. Its singleton fallback is conditioned on having at most one in every region, while the King’s region is protected. It provides no explicit no-piece procedure, or fallback for a player with a protected pair and only eligible singletons.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: There can be no permitted disk choice satisfying the printed selection condition. No source-backed substitute execution is available.

source_limitations.description: Secret removal of all from one region exempts a player with no pieces in any region, but does not explain selection when the player’s only regional pieces occupy the protected King’s region.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: The player has pieces in a region but cannot legally remove them or select an eligible occupied region.

source_limitations.description: Both secret-removal card headings and card faces address fellow players, whereas the detailed paragraphs say all players simultaneously select regions. The source does not reconcile the selecting player’s disk participation.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: Who must perform the secret selection is ambiguous. The summary reports both formulations and does not silently change the card’s stated removal targets.

source_limitations.description: The general action rule permits any or all moved Caballeros to go to Castillo. The forced Movement card uses secret disks, which omit Castillo, without explicitly reconciling that general permission.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: Whether and how an affected player may send the forced group into Castillo cannot be settled definitively from these pages. The summary describes the printed disk procedure and separately flags the unresolved conflict.

source_limitations.description: All-4 special scoring refers to all regions whose first value is four and mobile scoreboards override printed values. A 4/0/0 scoreboard may be placed at Castillo; the source does not expressly state Castillo’s inclusion or exclusion for this combination. The all-5 card explicitly excludes Castillo.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: A reachable scoreboard placement creates an unresolved special-scoring inclusion question; the summary flags it instead of asserting an exception.

source_limitations.description: The Court says to move two own Caballeros from provinces to court, without an explicit shortfall rule. The ordinary power-card recruitment shortage rule is described separately and is not expressly extended to this special action.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: If provinces contain fewer than two, the source does not explicitly supply the missing execution procedure. The summary preserves this limitation.

source_limitations.description: Multi-origin four-piece intrigue effects say other regions, while some three-piece effects say any regions. No example defines whether other excludes each piece’s own origin or every selected origin collectively.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no definitive missing procedure invented.
source_limitations.impact: A strict universal ban on all selected origins as destinations would be an unsupported additional rule. The summary preserves the destination wording and explicitly declines that extra inference.

source_limitations.description: The King returns heading says fellow players, but both the detailed execution paragraph and card face say each player. Page 7 directs readers to detailed explanations when meaning is unclear.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Transparently follows each player, including the selecting player, and states the conflicting heading.
source_limitations.impact: This is a supported, disclosed use of the detailed explanation and matching card face, rather than an unsupported conflict resolution.

source_limitations.description: The source names the player furthest on the success track as winner and gives no additional endgame tiebreaker.
source_limitations.summary_treatment: Accurately states that no additional tiebreaker is supplied.

claims: 1996 base edition; Wolfgang Kramer and Richard Ulrich; 2–5 players; standard nine rounds around two hours; Jay Tummelson translation/editing attribution.

Five Grandes; 155 Caballeros/31 per color, including scoring marker; King and round marker; 65 power cards numbered 1–13; recruitment pictures 0–6; 45 action cards in 11/11/11/11/1 stacks; nine region cards; five disks; Castillo; mobile scoreboards 8/4/0 and 4/0/0.

King chosen by first revealed shuffled region card; players draw home regions and place Grandes; two home Caballeros, one score marker, seven court; remainder provinces; thirteen power cards and disk per player; shuffle stacks separately; start marker at 1.

Five actions revealed each round; chosen initial power-card starter; last turn player begins subsequent rounds; clockwise unique power values; used cards face up with only top visible; turns descending in value.

Recruit up to power allowance before selecting action; eligible own board pieces may make up province shortage; King and Castillo origin protections remain; court recruitment and board deployment are distinct.

Ordinary deployment and optional special action may occur in either order; neither may be split; ordinary deployment comes from court, up to stack number, divided among King-adjacent regions and Castillo; taking a card to prevent its special action is allowed.
Chosen action unavailable to later players; unused face-up actions discarded; King card returns each round.
King’s region bars Caballero, Grande and mobile-scoreboard movement both in and out, yet remains scoreable; King movement changes the protected region and current ordinary-deployment destinations.

Castillo placement allowed regardless of King; announce inserted quantity; pieces leave only at general scoring; special Castillo scoring uncovers and re-covers the same pieces without redistribution.

All-own-from-one-region intrigue distributes own pieces, with express permission to return some to origin; two additional court pieces have unrestricted non-King regional destinations; combined card chooses one of these specials.
Five-piece intrigue uses one origin, own and/or foreign pieces, and other regional destinations/ Castillo; three-foreign and any-three permit multiple eligible origins and any eligible destinations.

Two-own plus two-foreign preserves separate ownership allowances and multiple eligible origins; four-own permits own only; any-four permits either ownership; other-regions wording preserved for four-piece effects; no pieces taken from protected origins.

Veto lasts current or next round, stops one incomplete special or its remainder, cannot undo completed parts or stop ordinary deployment; announced special may be stopped before execution; discard on use or end of next round.
Both Decay cards affect fellow players’ courts and return pieces to provinces; all-court empty case and three-court fewer-than-three case handled as expressly specified.

The King returns follows detailed execution and card face: each player including selector, beginning left and clockwise, chooses three own pieces from regions/court but not King/Castillo; conflict and missing shortfall rule disclosed.
Selecting player chooses one regional Caballero of each player including self to return to owner’s provinces; no court/King/Castillo origins; absent-piece procedure not invented.

Both secret-removal specials use simultaneous secret disks and own pieces returned to provinces; remove-two normal and singleton criteria retained; remove-all zero-regional-piece exemption retained; participation and protected-only gaps disclosed.
Stack-2 pick-one-region scoring includes King and Castillo and uses normal scoring; special Castillo scoring does not empty it.

Stack-3 all-4, all-5 and all-6/7 region sets and nine printed regional values match; mobile values replace printed values and change eligibility; applicable bonuses retained; all-5 explicitly excludes Castillo.

Castillo-only scoring covers pieces again; first-position-only excludes Castillo and pays nothing for a first-place tie; most scores every tied regional total; least scores every tied nonempty minimum; both exclude Castillo from comparison and scoring.
Stack-3 choose-any-region includes King and Castillo; normal scoring and no Castillo redistribution.
Mobile scoreboard may enter board or change region, including Castillo; cannot enter/leave King’s region, stack with the other board, or be rotated/reversed.
Royal Adviser moves King to a neighboring region, at most one region away.

Forced Movement affects all fellow players’ pieces in selected region; simultaneous disk destinations; King/origin disk choice returns own group to court; no taking from protected King or Castillo; Castillo destination conflict separately disclosed.
Grande movement excludes King/Castillo destinations and cannot leave King’s region; multiple Grandes may coexist; new location becomes own home region.

Recover one played power card including current-turn card; no obligation to reveal; top-card recovery visible; Court special is two province-to-court pieces, separate from normal up-to-four deployment.
All-player secret scoring uses disks, hence nine board regions including King but excluding Castillo; simultaneous reveal; score uniquely chosen regions only.
Stack-5 King special may choose any region except Castillo; up-to-five ordinary deployment remains a separate activity with destinations based on current King.

General scoring after rounds 3/6/9; select hidden disk destinations before revealing Castillo, score Castillo, redistribute to one selected region per player, then score nine regions in track order; King destination prohibited and illegal selection sends group to court.

Only Caballeros count; Grandes identify home without adding majority strength; two-player only first, three-player first two, four/five first three; tie drops tied group one rank; supplied three-way-first and tied-third examples reproduced correctly.
King’s +2 and own-Grande home +2 awarded to sole majority, never a first-place tie; bonuses apply to special as well as general scoring.
Game ends after completed third general scoring; furthest success-track marker wins; no source tiebreaker invented.
